Absence of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ ions in the sarcoplasm

Continuous presence of high $\text{Ca}^{++}$ ions or depletion of acetylcholinesterase would cause continuous cross-bridge cycling (repeated attachment and detachment), provided ATP is available. Absence of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ ions would prevent the initial attachment of myosin to actin by keeping the active sites masked.
